rebaseline_note:
mcp_schemas 4271 -> 4860 (+13.8%), and the attribution is 100% THIS BRANCH with ZERO inherited share -- which is the opposite of the two entries below, so it is stated in that direction. road-to-a-graph-that-is-shipped 4.1 registers five code-graph MCP tools (graph_impact, graph_tests_for, graph_dead, graph_query, graph_path), taking the catalogue 31 -> 36.

MEASURED BY SUBSTITUTION, never estimated, using the method the eager_rule_load entry below records. origin/main's versions of the four files that define this surface (mcp_server/tools.ts, mcp_server/tool_catalog_source.ts, mcp_server/consumer_tool_catalog.json, build_mcp_catalog.ts) were put back and mcp_server/graph_tools.ts removed, with everything else on the branch left in place; `task audit-tokens` plus the gate then report mcp_schemas 4271 -- EXACTLY the baseline, +0.0%. So nothing on main moved this metric while the branch was in review, and the whole +589 is the branch's. Restored and re-measured at 4860 to confirm the substitution round-tripped.

TRIMMED FIRST, to the point of diminishing return, before any re-anchor was considered. Three passes over the five tools' descriptions and their per-property schema prose moved the five tools' own cost 855 -> 692 -> 635 -> 626 exact-BPE tokens, i.e. -163, -57, -9. The third pass moving 9 tokens is the signal this file's discipline names: the cost is no longer prose. What remains is 420 tokens of JSON SCHEMA STRUCTURE -- `type`, `minimum`, `default`, `required`, `additionalProperties` and the property names -- which is API surface rather than text, and shrinking it would mean removing parameters rather than words. Net effect on the gate: 5092 (+19.2%) -> 4860 (+13.8%), so the trim paid for 232 of the 821 the branch first cost, 28%.

Why the remaining 589 is not shrinkable further by prose: the five descriptions are now 206 tokens between them, an average of 41 each, and they still have to carry the two things a caller cannot discover by trying -- that graph_dead REFUSES with status `refused` rather than returning an empty list, and that graph_impact runs `git diff` and is therefore not read-only. Dropping either is how a caller reads a refusal as "nothing is dead", which is the exact false negative the verb was built to prevent.

The alternative to raising this baseline is not a smaller surface, it is five tools nobody can reach: Risk-Register rank 1 of that roadmap is "the install grows and the graph is still unread", and these tools are the readers. Standing cost is recorded separately and in the same spirit at agents/evidence/metrics/mcp-tool-standing-cost.jsonl (kernel tools/list 3,886 -> 4,876 tokens, appended rather than overwritten), and docs/CLAIMS.md's mcp-registered-server-standing-cost claim was restated to the new figure in the same change rather than left to age.

eager_rule_load, thin_rule_load, skill_descriptions and command_descriptions are NOT re-anchored in this pass: they read +2.3%, -1.9%, +3.0% and +2.5%. Three are inside tolerance and one is BELOW its baseline, and re-anchoring a passing metric while raising a failing one is how a ratchet quietly loses its grip on the surfaces that were fine -- the sentence the entry below already makes, applied to a different four. Note that thin_rule_load at -1.9% would be a legitimate LOWERING on its own reading; it is left alone because this branch did not earn it, and a drive-by tighten on a metric this branch does not touch is not this change's to make.

--- previous note, kept ---

thin_rule_load 15855 -> 18573 (+17.1%), and this one is a DEFINITION change rather than growth: road-to-trigger-delivered-rule-bodies step 1.3 stopped thinning the four rules the router gives no trigger at all (no-roadmap-references, rule-type-governance, skill-quality, source-confidentiality). They now project full-bodied, +2,871 exact-BPE tokens, and the projector NAMES them and their token sum on every --measure run instead of absorbing them into the pointer count.

Why the old number was wrong rather than merely smaller: a thin entry is a pointer that says 'load the body on trigger-match', and a rule with no trigger can never be matched. Thinning those four replaced a body with a promise nothing could keep -- a silent hole in the projection, not a saving. 15,855 was measuring a projection that could not be restored; 18,573 measures one that can. Every price row in internal/bench/reports/thin-inject-2026-08-23.md uses the honest figure, and the delivery arm still prices at $0.7285 against eager's $4.0335 per 50-turn x 5-spawn session, so the correction costs the conclusion nothing.

Shrinking something else until the number fit was not considered: there is nothing to shrink -- the delta is four bodies that must be present. The alternative to raising this baseline is keeping a projection that drops them, which is the defect the step exists to close.

eager_rule_load, skill_descriptions, command_descriptions and mcp_schemas are NOT re-anchored in this pass: they read +1.8%, +1.2%, +0.7% and +0.0%, all inside tolerance, and re-anchoring a passing metric while raising a failing one is how a ratchet quietly loses its grip on the surfaces that were fine.

--- previous note, kept ---

eager_rule_load 112694 -> 118428, itemised rather than silently raised, same discipline as the two previous re-anchors. +5734 total, of which THIS branch is 436 and 5298 is inherited growth that accumulated on main across four merges while this branch was in review.

The 436 is MEASURED, not estimated, and the method is cheap enough to repeat: this branch changes exactly one always-loaded rule projection (dist/agent-src/rules/decision-revisit-gate.md), so substituting main's version of that one file and re-running the gate reports 117992 (+4.7%) against 118428 (+5.1%) with it. The difference is the branch's whole contribution to this metric. Nothing else this branch touches is eager: the new gate, the census wiring and the sweep artifact are all outside the rule projection.

So the ceiling was crossed JOINTLY and the split is worth stating in that direction: main alone sits at +4.7%, already most of the way through the 5% allowance, and 436 tokens tipped it. Being the straw is not being the cause, but it is still this branch's 436.

What the 436 buys, since an always-loaded rule is the most expensive surface in the tree: the rule claimed `adr_cite_check` prints all seven step-2 reads while it printed four, so reads 5 and 7 were not performable from the tool the rule points an agent at. It now claims six and names why the seventh (reversibility of the proposed transition) belongs to the agent rather than to any tool. The field-by-field detail deliberately did NOT go into this rule, nor into the skill it routes to: the rule sits 2 lines under a hard 200-line cap and decision-review/SKILL.md 1 line under a 400-line warning threshold, where a 35-line addition turned a 0-warning tree into 1. It went into adr_cite_check.ts's module docstring, which has no line cap and is read by whoever runs the tool.

Shrinking the prose until the number fit was considered and rejected: the same convention this note follows records 'the fix was not to shrink the comments until the number fit' for the sibling size-budget ratchet, and the extraction that would be the honest alternative has nowhere to land (both candidate targets are at their caps, above). An itemised raise with a reproducible measurement is a one-line diff a maintainer can audit; a silently shaved rule is not.

thin_rule_load 15653 -> 15855 (+1.3%) is re-anchored in the same pass so the next reader compares against one measurement rather than a mix of dates. The three unchanged surfaces (skill_descriptions, command_descriptions, mcp_schemas) moved 0.0% and are left as they are.
